content:
Angles, triangles, circles and Euler's formula — Class 5 geometry rewards exact facts and clean diagrams. Here is what the IMO Class 5 geometry chapter tests, the facts to know cold, and a free 10-question test with figures.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Geometry — Angles and Shapes chapter tests

  • Angle types, complements and supplements
  • Triangle angle-sum and triangle types
  • Circles — radius, diameter, chord and circumference (π = 22/7)
  • Polygons, symmetry and Euler's formula for solids

Key facts your child should know

  • Complementary angles add to 90°; supplementary to 180°.
  • The angles of every triangle total 180°.
  • d = 2r and C = 2πr — with π = 22/7, r = 7 gives C = 44.
  • Euler's formula: F + V − E = 2 for every polyhedron.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up complement (90°) and supplement (180°).
  • Forgetting a triangle can have at most one right/obtuse angle.
  • Using the radius where the diameter is needed.

questions.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle measures
Two angles form a straight line. If one measures 77°, the other measures
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line total 180°: 180 − 77 = 103°.

questions.q: The longest chord that can be drawn in a circle is its
questions.explanation: A chord through the centre is the diameter — no other chord of the circle can be longer.

questions.q: In triangle PQR, angle P = 28° and angle Q = 105°. What is the measure of angle R?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180°: angle R = 180° − (28° + 105°) = 180° − 133° = 47°.

questions.q: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, i.e. 6° per minute. In 30 minutes it turns 30 × 6° = 180°.
